newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end with slight gains in apathetic trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end with slight gains in apathetic trade.

text.p: Shares on the Lima Stock Exchange closed up slightly in low volume, as investors adopted a wait- and-see tactic ahead of the publishing of macroeconomic indicators in Brazil late Tuesday, brokers said.
Trade in Lima usually follows trends in the region where Brazil has much weight.
Brokers expected Lima trade to be thin again Tuesday.
Monday, the General Index rose 0.05 percent to 2,014.41 points as the blue-chip Selective Index rose 0.04 percent to 2897.62 points, preliminary figures showed.
In a total of 1,546 operations, volume was 20 million soles ($7.6 million).

"All foreign (investors) are waiting for the current account balance numbers from Brazil," said Alberto Arispe of the local Macrovalores brokerage. "It will be the determining factor for regional markets."

He added that, in Lima, last week's publishing of a 0.83 percent July inflation figure, solid second quarter company financial results and the dissipation of political tensions would likely benefit the local market this week.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru made slight gains with a 0.81 percent rise to 6.26 soles on low volume of 404,000 shares.
The big winners were miner Milpo, which rose 4.29 percent to 36.50 soles on volume of 18,000 shares, and Peru's leading bank Credicorp, which rose 3.95 percent to $19.75 on volume of 38,500 shares.
Losers included Peruvian electricity generator Edegel -- down 3.74 percent to 1.03 soles on 145,000 shares -- and electricity distributor Edelnor -- down 2.23 percent to 1.75 soles on 15,000 shares.
